s: Two minutes on how the dock works and how to stay safe in the river. Your door code is at the end.
Free lot across from the marina at NE Bridgeton and NE 2nd. Follow the signs down the ramp to the dock.
check: Is this the ramp guests use? Docs say the lot is across from the East Ramp. No gate on the ramp today.

s: The sauna boat sits beside the lounge on the main dock. Everything is a short walk on the same dock.
check: Which end is upstream? None of the photos show the current. Tell me and I'll mark the flow on the map slide.

h: The landing deck and the dock past it
s: Hang out on the landing deck. The dock past it has a ladder at the far end. The private saunas are being built beyond that.
check: Security-camera view, fisheye. Is that the ladder you meant on the downstream dock?

s: Change rooms and the bathroom are here. Hang your coat and bag on the hooks. Shoes stay on the bench.
check: No lockers on site (lockers were dropped). Say so in the video, or leave it out?

s: Snacks are fine out here and on the roof. Only water goes in the sauna. No alcohol on site.
Bare feet on the boat. Your door code opens the keypad.

h: Steam: one scoop at a time
s: Ask the room first, then pour. Fresh water only. Don't touch the stove, the rocks, or the controls.
check: Stove is natural gas. Never say wood-fired.

s: Pull the cord for a cold rinse between rounds.
check: Photo is from June. Same spot today?

s: Dark, windy, too cold, not a strong swimmer? Skip the river. The sauna is the whole visit.
No staff. No lifeguard. You look after each other.
check: Camera still, low-res. Better photo of the sign?

s: A life jacket or swim buoy on everyone who goes in. No matter how well you swim.
check: Where will guest vests or buoys hang? Today they're only with the kayaks, and the PFD may still be missing after the theft.

s: Three ways out: the stair end of the boat, the far corner of the boat, and the dock downstream. Find them before you get in.
check: Docs say the east boat ladder is buckling and a new 5-step ladder is on order. Any ladder moving?

s: Cold water makes you gasp. Hold the ladder and breathe slow until it passes.
check: Is this our dock or the swim-event pier?

s: Never fight the current. Ride it to the nearest ladder.
check: Once you tell me the flow direction I'll add an arrow here.

h: Feet first, away from the boat
s: No diving. Push off hard so the current can't pull you under the hull.
check: Capitol safety plan v3 says ladders only. The video says feet-first jumps are OK. Insurer wording needs to match.

h: Off the roof? Take the stairs
s: Use the stairs, not the rail. Look below before you jump, and know which ladder you'll swim to.
Never alone in the river. Someone on the dock has eyes on you the whole time.
check: Same question as the gasp slide: our dock or another pier?

s: Throw the ring or reach with the rescue pole, then pull them to a ladder. Never go in after someone.
check: No photo of the rescue pole yet. Send one and I'll pin it. Doc says it hangs flat inside the pier rail next to the ring.

s: Shorter when the water is cold. Get out before you go numb.
check: Instagram cover frame with a play icon. OK for a draft?

s: No alcohol. Walk, don't run. Not after dark or in fog. Dizzy? Sit down and stay out of the water.
check: Open 6 AM to 10 PM. Is the river closed after dark, or just discouraged?

s: Two private saunas and a fire pit on the new float. Concept only: final finishes may change.
check: Keep this in the safety intro, or save it for a separate teaser?

s: Everyone signs their own waiver before you arrive. Your door code is in your booking.
check: Docs disagree on whether the code waits for every waiver. I used the newest wording.
